newsitem.title: UK: Microsoft Network sets 2nd UK ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Microsoft Network sets 2nd UK ad campaign.

text.p: Microsoft Corp, the U.S. software giant fighting for share in the crowded Internet service provider market, said it plans to launch a new UK advertising campaign for the Microsoft Network.
"The second wave is slated to start in April," Taylor Collyer, marketing director of Microsoft Network in the UK, told Reuters in an interview.
"It will be a little more aggressive than the first wave," he said.

Microsoft Network's first advertising campaign in Britain was launched in early December, using front-page advertisements in top British newspapers as part of efforts to double the network's UK subscriber base over the next 12 months.
The second wave of adverts will be launched in mid-April and will coincide with the next Microsoft product upgrade.
The new ad campaign, including newspaper and magazine ads, will run about four months, compared to the two-month campaign run previously.
Collyer said the four-month effort will be a "multi-million pound campaign." He declined to specify the spending plan, but said it will be under 10 million pounds.
Microsoft, which has run television ads in the U.S. for its Internet service, decided against advertising the Microsoft Network on British television.
"In the U.S. they are doing MSN (Microsoft Network) ads on television because the market is ready to support it," Collyer said. "But the market is not that developed here."

Only about 17 percent of British homes are equipped with personal computers compared to more than 40 percent in the U.S. Most home computers in the U.S. can dial into the Internet, but in Europe fewer than four percent of home PC users have Internet access.
As a result, Microsoft's television strategy in the UK will continue to focus on general brand advertising that also mentions the Microsoft Network, Collyer said.

Microsoft Network currently has about 110,000 subscribers in the UK, out of about 600,000 individual subscribers to the Internet in Britain. CompuServe Corp is the largest Internet provider in Britain.
